limitations: Only the locked zero-relocation gpuReadWrite fixture is mapped; arbitrary relocations and untrusted general ELF loading remain rejected. The mapped VA is image-relative and segment permissions are not enforced.
The negative mapping cases prove pre-allocation rejection and unchanged allocation/lease counters; copy/zero failure rollback and cross-context teardown are not generic loader claims.

The mapper stops at functional bytes and descriptor/entry addresses. It does not construct kernarg or AQL, publish a queue, connect HSAPacketProcessor/GPUDispatcher/ComputeUnit, or execute ISA instructions.
The retained VEGA_X86 regressions are compatibility evidence for reused state machines, not a dependency of the host-native target.
Triton end-to-end and Qwen3.5-0.8B inference both remain 0/1; no full ROCm, OpenCL CTS, hardware, timing, or performance claim is made.
result: The CP17-A PT_LOAD target builds with mold/24, passes staged-image, exact segment, BSS, descriptor-entry, pre-allocation rejection, lifetime, and no-x86 audits, and retains the CP16 native and VEGA_X86 state regressions. The next execution boundary remains dynamic kernarg/AQL and the real GPU pipeline.
